title: Ensure access to build process triggering is minimized
description: A remote trigger token is a shared secret in a URL: anyone who has ever seen it can start this build, from anywhere, with no account and no audit trail naming them. URLs leak — into logs, browser history, chat messages — and a leaked one cannot be traced or individually revoked. Triggering should go through Jenkins' own authorization, where it is per-user and logged.
remediation: Job -> Configure -> Build Triggers: untick "Trigger builds remotely" and remove the authentication token. Replace callers with an authenticated request from a service account (POST /job/<name>/build with an API token and its user's Job/Build permission), or with an SCM webhook, both of which are attributable and revocable per caller. The permission matrix governing who may trigger builds is not exposed by any API and still needs review by hand.
fixSummary: Untick "Trigger builds remotely" at Configure -> Build Triggers and remove the token.
